question: A millwright is performing a routine gearbox inspection. The gearbox has a plugged breather vent on the top cover that has not been serviced in over a year. What problem does a plugged gearbox breather vent cause during normal thermal cycling of the gearbox in service?

options.A: Pressure buildup inside the gearbox that forces oil past the shaft seals.
options.B: Excessive cooling of the gearbox oil that increases viscosity beyond design.
options.C: Contaminated air entering the gearbox through the breather during cool-down.
options.D: Oil foaming caused by air pressure fluctuations acting on the oil surface.

explanation: When a gearbox heats up during operation, air inside expands and pressure rises. If the breather is plugged, this pressure cannot vent and instead pushes oil past the path of least resistance, which is usually the shaft seals. The resulting external oil leaks are often misdiagnosed as seal failure when the actual cause is a plugged breather. Breather condition is a key item on every routine gearbox inspection checklist.

question: A process engineer mentions that a new pump has a high suction specific speed value. A millwright maintaining this pump should know that high suction specific speed indicates increased susceptibility to which pump operating problem at low flow rates?

options.A: Suction recirculation leading to cavitation damage at low flow conditions.
options.B: Discharge recirculation causing high vibration at maximum flow conditions.
options.C: Bearing overload caused by excessive radial thrust at design flow rate.
options.D: Shaft seal leakage caused by high suction pressure at low flow rates.

explanation: Pumps with high suction specific speed values are more susceptible to suction recirculation at low flow rates, which can cause vibration, noise, and erosive cavitation damage to the impeller and casing near the suction inlet. Suction specific speed is used by engineers to evaluate this risk when selecting pumps. Millwrights should avoid operating high suction specific speed pumps at very low flow rates for extended periods.

question: A millwright is servicing a cooling tower at an industrial facility during a scheduled shutdown. Which cooling tower component increases heat transfer efficiency by maximizing contact surface area between falling water and rising air?

options.A: The fill media installed in the tower air and water contact zone.
options.B: The drift eliminators installed at the air outlet near the tower top.
options.C: The makeup water float valve installed in the collection basin.
options.D: The fan blade assembly installed at the tower top or bottom inlet.

explanation: Fill media is the structured plastic or wood material inside the cooling tower that breaks falling water into thin films and small droplets, dramatically increasing the contact surface area between water and the rising air stream. More contact area means more evaporative cooling per unit of water flow. Drift eliminators remove water droplets from exiting air to reduce water loss from the tower.

question: A millwright is selecting a replacement piston seal for a hydraulic cylinder operating at 200 bar and 0.3 metres per second piston speed. Which piston seal type is preferred for dynamic hydraulic cylinder applications at normal industrial operating speeds?

options.A: A lip seal or U-cup seal designed for dynamic reciprocating motion.
options.B: A standard O-ring without any backup rings at the piston groove.
options.C: A cast iron piston ring designed for very high temperature operation.
options.D: A face seal designed for static flange connection sealing applications.

explanation: Lip seals and U-cup seals are preferred for dynamic piston seal applications in hydraulic cylinders because their geometry allows fluid pressure to energize the sealing lip for better sealing under load. O-rings are better suited to static or very low-speed dynamic applications. Cast iron piston rings are used only in very high temperature or special duty cylinders where elastomeric seals cannot survive.

question: A millwright is taking a hydraulic oil sample to send to a laboratory for condition monitoring analysis. From which location in the hydraulic circuit should the oil sample be taken for the most accurate and representative condition monitoring results?

options.A: From a live sampling valve on the return line before the reservoir filter.
options.B: From the drain plug at the very bottom of the hydraulic reservoir.
options.C: From the highest point in the pressure line after the main pump outlet.
options.D: From the reservoir vent or breather cap opening at the top of the tank.

explanation: Oil samples for condition monitoring must be taken from a live point in the circulating hydraulic circuit, ideally from a dedicated sampling valve on the return line before the filter. Sampling before the filter captures particles generated in the circuit before they are removed. Sampling from the drain plug at the bottom of the reservoir collects settled sediment that is not representative of the circulating oil condition.

question: A millwright is setting up a vibration data collection route for a new centrifugal fan installation. To ensure that trend data collected over time is comparable from one collection visit to the next, which conditions must be identical during every vibration data collection visit?

options.A: Same operating load, speed, sensor location, and sensor mounting method.
options.B: Same ambient temperature in the plant and same barometric pressure reading.
options.C: Same technician using the same instrument regardless of calibration date.
options.D: Same time of day to ensure the machine has been running for equal time.

explanation: Meaningful vibration trending requires that every data collection visit replicates the same operating conditions including load, speed, sensor placement, and sensor mounting method. Changes in any of these variables will produce changes in vibration readings that are not related to the machine's actual mechanical condition. Standardizing these parameters is the foundation of a reliable predictive maintenance vibration program.

question: A worker is developing a task hazard analysis for cleaning the inside of a mixing vessel that contains rotating agitator blades and was previously used to store a flammable solvent. Which hazard must be ranked as the highest priority to control before any entry?

options.A: Slip and fall hazard from residual solvent coating the vessel floor.
options.B: Ergonomic hazard from working in a confined, awkward posture inside the vessel.
options.C: Atmospheric hazard from flammable vapors or oxygen deficiency inside the confined space.
options.D: Mechanical hazard from the agitator blades if someone rotates the shaft externally.

explanation: Confined space entry standards rank atmospheric hazards as the highest priority because flammable vapors or oxygen-deficient air can kill a worker within seconds of entry, before any other hazard can be addressed. Atmospheric testing and continuous ventilation must be completed and confirmed before any person enters the vessel. The mechanical hazard of the agitator is controlled second through lockout, but atmospheric safety is always the first gate for confined space entry.

question: A torque specification chart shows that a Grade 8 metric M16 bolt with a standard coarse thread requires 150 Nm of torque when using clean, dry threads. A millwright is using a torque wrench calibrated in foot-pounds. Which value should be set on the wrench to achieve 150 Nm?

options.A: Set the wrench to approximately 111 ft-lb using the conversion factor 1 Nm equals 0.738 ft-lb.
options.B: Set the wrench to approximately 203 ft-lb since 1 ft-lb equals approximately 0.74 Nm.
options.C: Set the wrench to 150 ft-lb because metric Nm values are numerically equal to ft-lb values.
options.D: Set the wrench to 130 ft-lb by subtracting 20 for the metric-to-imperial conversion factor.

explanation: The conversion from Newton-metres to foot-pounds uses the factor 1 Nm equals 0.7376 ft-lb. Multiplying 150 Nm by 0.7376 gives approximately 110.6 ft-lb, which rounds to 111 ft-lb. Setting the torque wrench to 111 ft-lb will apply the correct 150 Nm of torque to the M16 bolt without over-tightening or under-tightening the fastener.

question: The two-leg sling diagram shows a 4,000 kg load suspended at a sling angle of 30 degrees from vertical. Each sling leg has an equal share of the load. What is the tension acting on each sling leg?

options.A: Approximately 1,732 kg per leg.
options.B: Approximately 2,000 kg per leg, using simple load division.
options.C: Approximately 2,309 kg per leg, accounting for sling angle.
options.D: Approximately 4,619 kg per leg, at this acute sling angle.

explanation: Tension per leg equals half the load divided by the cosine of the sling angle from vertical: (4,000 / 2) / cos(30 degrees) = 2,000 / 0.866 = 2,309 kg. Option B ignores the angle effect, which understates tension and can lead to sling overload. Options A and D apply incorrect formulas.

question: The V-belt drive in the diagram has a 300 mm driver sheave at 1,440 RPM and a 600 mm driven sheave. What is the speed ratio, and what is the driven sheave speed?

options.A: 2:1 step-up, 2,880 RPM driven speed.
options.B: 1:1 ratio, 1,440 RPM driven speed.
options.C: 3:1 reduction, 480 RPM driven speed.
options.D: 2:1 reduction, 720 RPM driven speed.

explanation: Speed ratio = driven diameter / driver diameter = 600 / 300 = 2:1 reduction; driven speed = 1,440 x (300 / 600) = 720 RPM. The driven sheave is twice the diameter, so it turns at half the speed while producing twice the torque. Options A and B invert the ratio or ignore it; option C applies a 3:1 factor not supported by the given diameters.

question: A chain drive has a 20-tooth driver sprocket running at 1,200 RPM and a 60-tooth driven sprocket as shown. What is the speed ratio of this drive and the driven sprocket speed?

options.A: 3:1 reduction, 400 RPM driven speed.
options.B: 3:1 step-up, 3,600 RPM driven speed.
options.C: 2:1 reduction, 600 RPM driven speed.
options.D: 1:3 ratio, 900 RPM driven speed.

explanation: Speed ratio = driven teeth / driver teeth = 60 / 20 = 3:1 reduction; driven speed = 1,200 x (20 / 60) = 400 RPM. The larger sprocket always turns slower in a single-stage chain drive when it has more teeth than the driver. Options B, C, and D apply wrong tooth ratios or invert the speed relationship.

question: The chain drive in the diagram uses a 25-tooth driver sprocket at 900 RPM and a 50-tooth driven sprocket. What is the output speed at the driven sprocket shaft?

options.A: 900 RPM.
options.C: 450 RPM.
options.D: 225 RPM.

explanation: Output speed = 900 x (25 / 50) = 450 RPM. The driven sprocket has twice the teeth, so it turns at exactly half the speed of the driver, a 2:1 reduction. Options A and B ignore the tooth ratio; option D invents a friction loss that does not apply to the speed ratio calculation.

question: A process pump has a suction pressure of 20 kPa absolute and adds 250 kPa of differential pressure across the impeller. A technician needs to determine the discharge pressure to set a downstream pressure relief valve. What is the pump discharge pressure?

options.A: 230 kPa absolute, by subtracting the suction pressure from the differential pressure added.
options.B: 125 kPa absolute, by averaging the suction pressure and the pump differential pressure together.
options.C: 250 kPa absolute.
options.D: 270 kPa absolute, by adding the suction pressure of 20 kPa to the pump differential of 250 kPa.

explanation: Pump discharge pressure equals the suction pressure plus the differential pressure the pump adds across the impeller. Adding the suction pressure of 20 kPa absolute to the 250 kPa of pump differential gives a discharge pressure of 270 kPa absolute. The downstream pressure relief valve should be set above the normal operating discharge pressure of 270 kPa but below the maximum allowable working pressure of the downstream piping system.

question: A millwright calculates net positive suction head available for a pump installation. Atmospheric pressure is 101.3 kPa, fluid vapor pressure is 12 kPa, static suction head equals 29.4 kPa, and friction losses in the suction line are 5 kPa. The pump requires a minimum NPSHr of 4.5 metres. Is this installation adequate?

options.A: No, the NPSHa is only 3.8 metres, which is below the required minimum of 4.5 metres.
options.B: Yes, NPSHa calculates to approximately 11.6 metres, which exceeds the 4.5 metre requirement.
options.C: Yes, but only if a booster pump is added to the suction line to increase available NPSH.
options.D: No, the friction losses of 5 kPa reduce NPSHa below the minimum threshold of 4.5 metres.

explanation: NPSHa is calculated as the sum of atmospheric pressure minus vapor pressure plus static suction head minus friction losses, all converted to metres of head. Adding 101.3 minus 12 plus 29.4 minus 5 gives 113.7 kPa, and dividing by 9.81 kPa per metre of water gives approximately 11.6 metres of NPSHa. Since 11.6 metres exceeds the required NPSHr of 4.5 metres with a large margin, the installation is adequate and cavitation risk is low.

question: A millwright is setting the impeller running clearance on a centrifugal pump using the wear ring adjustment method. The OEM specification calls for a clearance of 0.35 mm between the impeller and the wear ring. Describe the correct procedure to set this clearance.

options.A: Back off the gland bolts, insert a 0.35 mm feeler gauge between the impeller and casing, then retighten.
options.B: Install a new wear ring and bolt the casing closed since new wear rings are pre-set to OEM clearance.
options.C: Set clearance by filling the pump with oil and measuring the oil film pressure drop across the wear ring.
options.D: Adjust the impeller back by 3 mm, then advance it forward until contact, then back off to the feeler gauge specification.

explanation: The standard procedure for setting impeller clearance is to back the impeller away from the wear ring, then advance it slowly until the impeller just makes contact with the ring as a reference zero point. From the contact position, the impeller is backed off by the specified clearance amount, typically by rotating the adjusting nut, and then locked in position. A feeler gauge is then used to verify the gap is at the specified 0.35 mm before the pump is closed up.

question: A production pump experienced 4 failures requiring unplanned shutdown over a 12-month period. The plant runs the pump continuously 24 hours per day. The maintenance planner asks a millwright to calculate the mean time between failures for this pump.

options.A: MTBF equals 3 months, calculated by dividing 12 months by the 4 failures directly.
options.B: MTBF equals 2,160 hours, calculated by dividing total operating hours of 8,640 by 4 failures.
options.C: MTBF equals 720 hours, calculated using one month of operating hours divided by one failure.
options.D: MTBF equals 4,320 hours, calculated by dividing annual hours by half the number of failures.

explanation: Mean time between failures is calculated by dividing the total operating hours in the observation period by the number of failures that occurred during that period. Running continuously for 12 months gives 12 times 720 hours per month, which equals 8,640 total operating hours. Dividing 8,640 hours by 4 failures gives an MTBF of 2,160 hours, which is the average time the pump runs before experiencing another failure.

question: Before a lift, a millwright inspects a 6-strand wire rope sling and finds 4 broken wires in one strand within a single rope lay length. What is the correct action?

options.A: Use the sling for light lifts only and tag it for replacement within 30 days.
options.B: Replace only the damaged section by cutting and re-swaging the end.
options.C: Continue using the sling if no other strands show broken wires.
options.D: Remove the sling from service immediately and destroy or tag it condemned.

explanation: The removal-from-service criterion for a 6-strand wire rope sling is 3 or more broken wires in one strand within one rope lay length; finding 4 broken wires in one strand exceeds this limit. The sling must be removed from service immediately and should be cut or otherwise rendered unusable so it cannot be put back into service by someone else. Wire rope slings that exceed discard criteria are unpredictable under load and must never be used regardless of the load weight.

question: The bearing cross-section diagram labels the inner race, outer race, balls, and shaft bore. A shaft running at 1,450 RPM is supported by this bearing. Which labeled component rotates at the same speed as the shaft during normal operation?

options.A: The outer race.
options.B: The balls only.
options.C: The shaft bore and inner race together, rotating with the shaft.
options.D: All four labeled components rotate at shaft speed in service.

explanation: The inner race is press-fitted to the shaft and rotates at exactly shaft speed, while the shaft bore is simply the opening through which the shaft passes, so both move with the shaft. The outer race is press-fitted into the stationary housing and does not rotate. The balls rotate about their own axes and orbit around the bearing center, not at shaft speed. Option D is incorrect because only the inner components rotate with the shaft.

question: A millwright needs to set the system relief valve on a hydraulic circuit with a maximum operating pressure of 150 bar. How should the relief valve be set?

options.A: Set the relief valve to exactly 150 bar to match the maximum operating pressure.
options.B: Set the relief valve to 165 bar, which is 10 percent above maximum operating pressure.
options.C: Set the relief valve to 200 bar to ensure it never opens under normal operation.
options.D: Set the relief valve to 130 bar to provide a safety margin below maximum pressure.

explanation: The system relief valve must be set above the maximum working pressure so it does not open under normal operating conditions, but not so high that it fails to protect the system during a pressure spike or blocked actuator event. The standard practice is to set the relief valve 10 percent above the maximum system working pressure, giving 165 bar for a 150-bar system. Setting it too close to working pressure causes nuisance opening and heating; setting it too high reduces the overpressure protection for components rated at the working pressure.

question: A double-acting air cylinder extends fully but does not retract when the valve is shifted. A millwright begins systematic diagnosis. What is the correct first check?

options.A: Replace the cylinder immediately since failure to retract always means the rod seal has failed.
options.B: Verify the pilot signal is reaching the valve on the retract side before checking downstream components.
options.C: Increase the regulator pressure by 20 percent to overcome internal friction in the cylinder.
options.D: Check the extend port flow control for restriction before checking the valve or pilot signal.

explanation: When an actuator fails to move in one direction, the first check is to confirm the valve is actually receiving the correct pilot signal to shift to the retract position. If no pilot signal reaches the valve, the valve does not shift and no air is sent to the rod side of the cylinder. Confirming the signal first eliminates the upstream electrical and control circuit before focusing on the valve function, cylinder seals, and port blockage.

question: A millwright needs to check the nitrogen pre-charge pressure in a hydraulic accumulator. What must be done before connecting a gauge to the gas valve?

options.A: Increase hydraulic system pressure to full working pressure to stabilize the accumulator before testing.
options.B: Discharge the accumulator into the tank by rapidly cycling an actuator, then measure gas pressure immediately.
options.C: Leave the accumulator connected to the system to get an accurate combined pressure reading.
options.D: Isolate the accumulator from the hydraulic circuit and fully relieve oil pressure from the accumulator before gauging.

explanation: Before checking accumulator pre-charge, the accumulator must be isolated from the hydraulic circuit and all oil pressure must be fully relieved from the oil side of the accumulator. If oil pressure remains when the gas valve is opened, the reading will reflect combined oil and gas pressure, not the true pre-charge. Additionally, connecting a gauge to an accumulator under hydraulic pressure without isolation is a serious safety hazard that can result in high-pressure oil release.

question: A millwright completes a bearing replacement on a pump and must fill out the maintenance job report. What information is required in the report?

options.A: Technician name and total labour hours spent on the repair only.
options.B: As-found alignment readings, as-left alignment readings, bearing part number, hours on old bearing if known, and torque values applied.
options.C: Part cost, labour cost, and downtime duration for maintenance accounting purposes.
options.D: Equipment number, work order number, and supervisor approval signature only.

explanation: A complete maintenance job report for a bearing replacement must capture the as-found condition, including alignment readings taken before disassembly, and the as-left condition, including post-installation alignment and bearing fit readings. The replaced bearing part number creates a component history trail, and recording hours on the old bearing allows maintenance planners to refine the replacement interval. Torque values applied to locking hardware confirm the assembly was completed to specification and provide a record if a fastener is found loose during a future inspection.

question: Before using ratchet straps to secure a component during a mechanical assembly, a millwright must inspect each strap. Which condition found during inspection requires the strap to be immediately removed from service and not used for the lift?

options.A: Frayed webbing fibres, a bent ratchet hook, or any visible cut in the strap material.
options.B: Minor surface dirt on the webbing that can be wiped off before use.
options.C: A slightly stiff ratchet mechanism that operates normally after one or two cycles.
options.D: A faded colour label that is still readable under good lighting conditions.

explanation: Frayed webbing, cuts in the material, or a bent hook all directly reduce the rated working load limit of the strap and can lead to sudden failure during a lift. A strap with any of these defects must be tagged out and destroyed so it cannot be accidentally reused. Surface dirt, minor stiffness, and faded labels do not compromise structural integrity and do not require immediate removal from service.

question: A millwright must verify that a machined surface is square to a reference face using a combination square. After placing the square against the reference face and sliding the blade against the work surface, a feeler gauge is used to check the gap. Which procedure correctly interprets the feeler gauge reading in this application?

options.A: The thinnest feeler blade that slides in without force indicates the gap size at that point.
options.B: The thickest feeler blade that cannot be inserted indicates the exact gap measurement.
options.C: Any feeler blade that enters with moderate pressure gives an accurate gap reading.
options.D: Insert multiple blades simultaneously and read the gap as the sum of all thicknesses inserted.

explanation: The correct feeler gauge technique is to find the thickest blade that slides through the gap with light drag but without forcing, because that blade's thickness equals the gap dimension at that point. A blade that cannot enter without force is thicker than the gap; a blade that enters with no drag at all may be thinner than the gap, understating the measurement. This method gives a reliable, repeatable measurement for precision gap checks in millwright work.

question: A millwright must align a belt drive by checking that both sheaves are coplanar and properly aligned. A straightedge is laid across the face of both sheaves. What are the four contact points that must be checked to confirm the sheaves are in the same plane?

options.A: Both edges of the large sheave face and both edges of the small sheave face must all contact the straightedge simultaneously.
options.B: The top of the large sheave and the bottom of the small sheave must contact the straightedge with the other two edges floating.
options.C: One edge of each sheave is sufficient because if those two points align, the remaining two are automatically aligned.
options.D: The straightedge needs only to contact the outside face of each sheave at a single tangent point per sheave.

explanation: A straightedge placed across two sheaves must contact all four rim edges simultaneously to confirm the sheaves are in the same plane and parallel to each other. Gaps at any of the four contact points indicate either angular misalignment where the shafts are not parallel, or axial offset where the sheave faces are in parallel but offset planes. Checking only two contact points misses angular misalignment between the sheave planes, which causes rapid belt and sheave groove wear.

question: During a coupling grid inspection, a millwright removes the coupling cover and examines the grid element. The grid originally measured 8 mm thick in the new condition. The measured thickness during inspection is 5.8 mm. What action should the millwright take based on this measurement?

options.A: Replace the grid element because 5.8 mm represents 27.5% wear, which exceeds the 25% replacement threshold.
options.B: Continue using the grid because 5.8 mm is above 50% of original thickness and replacement is only needed below 50%.
options.C: Clean and re-lubricate the grid element and reinstall without replacement because wear below 30% is acceptable.
options.D: Replace the coupling grid only if visible cracks are present; thickness measurement alone is not a rejection criterion.

explanation: The standard replacement criterion for coupling grid elements is wear exceeding 25% of the original thickness. Original thickness is 8 mm, and 25% of 8 mm is 2 mm, so the replacement threshold is reached when thickness drops to 6 mm or below. At 5.8 mm, the element has worn 2.2 mm or 27.5%, which exceeds the 25% limit, and the grid must be replaced before it reaches the point of sudden failure and possible equipment damage.

question: A millwright must select a pump to transfer a slurry containing 30% abrasive solids by volume from a sump to a process tank. Which pump type is most appropriate for this service, and which common pump types must be avoided?

options.A: A heavy-duty slurry centrifugal or progressive cavity pump; avoid gear pumps and vane pumps because abrasives will rapidly erode the close-clearance surfaces.
options.B: A standard centrifugal pump with stainless steel impeller because high velocity provides adequate erosion resistance.
options.C: A gear pump with hardened gears because the positive displacement action handles high-solids fluids more reliably.
options.D: A vane pump with PTFE vanes because the vanes can deform around solid particles without damage.

explanation: Slurry centrifugal pumps are designed with thick wear-resistant impellers and casings with large internal clearances to tolerate abrasive particles without rapid erosion. Progressive cavity pumps handle high-viscosity abrasive slurries effectively through the elastomeric stator geometry. Gear pumps and vane pumps have precision close-clearance internal surfaces where hard particles cause rapid erosive wear, leading to internal leakage and loss of pump capacity within a short operating time.

question: A millwright is investigating a pneumatic system that shows a 40 kPa pressure drop between the compressor outlet and the end-use tool, even with no tools running. What is the correct procedure to trace the source of this pressure drop?

options.A: Use ultrasonic leak detection equipment to locate leaks at fittings and joints, identify the highest differential pressure leg, and check the filter and regulator for blockage or malfunction.
options.B: Increase the compressor set pressure by 40 kPa to compensate for the drop and document the adjusted setting in the maintenance log.
options.C: Replace all threaded fittings in the system with new fittings sealed with thread tape, then retest the pressure drop.
options.D: Remove the pressure regulator and bypass it temporarily to determine if the regulator is causing the restriction.

explanation: Ultrasonic detection identifies air leaks at fittings, valves, and connections by detecting the high-frequency sound of escaping compressed air that is inaudible at normal frequencies. After locating and quantifying leaks, the highest differential pressure leg is the circuit segment with the greatest restriction, which points to blockage in the filter bowl or regulator internals. Increasing compressor pressure does not solve the root cause and increases energy consumption and system stress without restoring proper delivery pressure.

question: A millwright is setting up a pneumatic pressure regulator for a new workstation. The application requires a minimum of 550 kPa at the tool inlet. The supply line pressure is 800 kPa. Where should the regulator outlet pressure be set to ensure reliable tool operation?

options.A: Set the regulator slightly above 550 kPa to ensure the tool receives at least the minimum pressure, without setting it at or near the maximum inlet pressure of 800 kPa.
options.B: Set the regulator to the maximum inlet pressure of 800 kPa to ensure maximum available force is delivered to the tool at all times.
options.C: Set the regulator to the midpoint between minimum and maximum, which would be 675 kPa for this application.
options.D: Leave the regulator at the factory default setting because it is calibrated by the manufacturer for general industrial use.

explanation: A regulator set to match or exceed inlet pressure bypasses the regulation function and exposes the tool and downstream components to full line pressure, which can exceed their rated specifications. Setting the regulator just above the minimum required pressure ensures the tool receives adequate supply while staying well within the rated pressure of hoses, fittings, and tool components downstream. The difference between the set point and the minimum tool requirement should account for any line losses between the regulator and the tool inlet.

question: A millwright is using a crane to land a heavy pump onto a sole plate. Just before the final descent, what is the most important positioning check that must be confirmed?

options.A: Confirm that the tag lines are taut and the pump is rotating slowly before landing.
options.B: Confirm that the crane load cell reads within 5% of the pump nameplate weight before descending.
options.C: Confirm that all workers are standing at least 3 metres from the sole plate during landing.
options.D: Confirm that the crane hook is directly above the center of gravity of the pump before descending.

explanation: If the crane hook is not directly above the load's center of gravity, the load will swing outward as soon as tension is applied and then snap back uncontrollably as it lifts or lowers, creating a serious strike hazard. Positioning the hook directly over the center of gravity ensures the load hangs plumb and descends vertically onto the sole plate without swinging. This check must be completed before the final descent, not corrected mid-air with tag lines.

question: During a load transfer between two crane operators, one of the workers on the ground gives an emergency stop signal. Which statement correctly describes how both crane operators must respond?

options.A: Only the signal person assigned to the lift has authority to give a stop signal during the transfer.
options.B: The operator currently moving the load obeys the stop signal; the standby operator continues normally.
options.C: An emergency stop signal from any person on the worksite takes immediate priority over all other signals.
options.D: Both operators pause and wait for the appointed signal person to confirm the emergency stop is valid.

explanation: Emergency stop is the one crane signal that overrides all other communications and must be obeyed immediately regardless of who gives it, whether a signal person, a worker on the ground, or anyone nearby. Both operators must stop all crane motion the moment an emergency stop is received and hold position until the hazard is assessed and a qualified person gives the all-clear. Delaying to confirm the signal with the appointed signal person wastes critical time when a person or load is at risk.

question: A millwright is selecting a gasket for a 150-pound ANSI flanged joint on a hot water line operating at 100 degrees Celsius. Which gasket material is appropriate for this service condition?

options.A: A rubber flat-face gasket.
options.B: A spiral-wound metallic gasket.
options.C: A compressed fibre or PTFE-enveloped gasket rated for the service temperature and pressure class.
options.D: A cork sheet gasket.

explanation: A 150-pound ANSI flange on a 100-degree Celsius hot water line requires a gasket that will remain stable and maintain its seating stress over the full operating temperature range without blowing out or compressing excessively. Compressed fibre sheet (such as aramid or synthetic fibre) and PTFE-enveloped gaskets are both rated for this temperature range and are compatible with hot water service. Standard rubber gaskets can soften and extrude at sustained temperatures near 100 degrees Celsius, making them unsuitable for this application.

question: A millwright is replacing a hydraulic piston pump. After installing the new pump and connecting all lines, what two steps must be completed before starting the prime mover?

options.A: Verify the pump rotation direction matches the shaft marking, then fill the pump case drain port with clean hydraulic oil before connecting the case drain line.
options.B: Install a new high-pressure filter element.
options.C: Bleed the pump suction line by cracking the suction fitting.
options.D: Verify the coupling alignment is within specification and install a new pump inlet strainer screen.

explanation: Piston pumps rely on hydraulic oil in the case to lubricate the internal rotating group from the first moment of operation. Running a piston pump dry even briefly can score the pistons, cylinder block, and valve plate, causing immediate and irreversible damage. Filling the case drain port with clean hydraulic oil before connecting the drain line ensures the internal components are lubricated on first rotation. Verifying correct rotation direction prevents the pump from operating backward, which can cause rapid failure of the inlet check valves and internal seals.

question: A millwright needs to test a pneumatic check valve removed from a compressed air circuit. What two tests confirm the valve is functioning correctly?

options.A: Apply air pressure from the upstream inlet side.
options.B: Apply air pressure from both directions simultaneously.
options.C: Submerge the valve in water and apply inlet pressure while watching for bubbles at the outlet port only.
options.D: Apply full system pressure from the outlet side only.

explanation: A check valve has two functional requirements: it must pass flow freely in the intended direction with minimal pressure drop, and it must block flow completely in the reverse direction. Testing from the upstream inlet confirms the valve opens at the rated cracking pressure and passes adequate flow. Testing from the downstream outlet confirms the poppet or ball seats completely against reverse pressure with zero leakage, which is the primary safety function of a check valve in a pneumatic circuit.

question: An equipment manual specifies grease with NLGI Grade 2, lithium complex thickener, and a minimum dropping point of 180 degrees C. The plant lubricant catalogue lists four greases. The millwright must select the correct one for a pillow block bearing operating at 120 degrees C continuous service temperature.

options.A: NLGI 2 lithium soap grease, dropping point 160C, EP additives included.
options.B: NLGI 3 lithium complex grease, dropping point 250C, no EP additives.
options.C: NLGI 2 lithium complex grease, dropping point 260C, EP additives included.
options.D: NLGI 1 lithium complex grease, dropping point 200C, EP additives included.

explanation: The manual specifies NLGI Grade 2 and lithium complex thickener with a minimum dropping point of 180C; all three criteria must be met simultaneously. Option C matches Grade 2 and lithium complex and exceeds the 180C dropping point at 260C, making it fully compliant. Options A and B fail on either the thickener type or the NLGI grade, and option D fails on the NLGI grade.

question: A millwright is assigned to replace a proximity sensor on a conveyor frame at 1.8 metres above the floor on a mezzanine with open grating and no permanent guardrail on the work side. The task will take approximately 20 minutes. What fall protection measure is required for this work?

options.A: No fall protection required because the task is short and the worker is experienced.
options.B: A spotter standing below the work area to warn other workers of any falling hazard.
options.C: Fall restraint or fall arrest system.
options.D: A safety cone barrier at floor level to keep other workers away from the work area below.

explanation: Provincial occupational health and safety regulations require fall protection for any work at or above 1.2 metres when there is no permanent guardrail. At 1.8 metres, the millwright must use either a fall restraint system (prevents reaching the edge) or a fall arrest system (stops a fall in progress). The duration or experience level of the worker does not reduce the legal requirement for fall protection.

question: A millwright rigs a two-leg wire rope bridle to lift a steel frame. Each sling leg has a WLL of 5 tonnes in a vertical hitch. The two legs form a 45-degree angle from horizontal at the load attachment points. What is the maximum allowable load the bridle can safely lift in this configuration?

options.A: 10 tonnes.
options.B: 3.54 tonnes.
options.C: 5 tonnes.
options.D: 7.07 tonnes.

explanation: When slings form an angle from horizontal, each leg supports a tension greater than the vertical load component; the allowable load equals WLL multiplied by the sine of the angle from horizontal. At 45 degrees, sin 45 equals 0.707, so each leg can safely carry 5 x 0.707 = 3.54 tonnes. Two legs together can carry 3.54 + 3.54 = 7.07 tonnes as the maximum allowable load.

question: A millwright plans to use a 3-tonne rated come-along to pull a 1,200 kg process pump horizontally across a concrete floor. The come-along anchor point is a structural column with a rated anchor plate. The pulling force needed is estimated at 600 kg due to friction. What must the millwright verify about the anchor point before applying load?

options.A: The anchor point must be rated for at least the weight of the pump, which is 1,200 kg.
options.B: The anchor point must be rated for the combined weight of the pump and the come-along.
options.C: The anchor point must be rated for the maximum force the come-along can develop, which is 3 tonnes.
options.D: The anchor point only needs to be rated for the estimated pulling force of 600 kg.

explanation: The anchor point must be rated for the maximum force the pulling device can generate, not just the estimated load. A come-along rated at 3 tonnes can develop up to 3 tonnes of force if operated to its mechanical limit, which could happen if the load sticks or the operator continues pulling. Sizing the anchor to the estimated 600 kg pulling force creates an unsafe condition if actual resistance exceeds the estimate.

question: A multi-stage gearbox was laser-aligned cold before startup. After 4 hours of continuous full-load operation the millwright wants to verify that thermal growth has not moved the shafts out of alignment. What is the correct method to check alignment under hot running conditions?

options.A: Shut down the gearbox and check alignment immediately after stopping while it is still hot.
options.B: Check bearing temperatures with a contact thermometer and use the readings to calculate thermal offset.
options.C: Use optical alignment tools or dial indicators to measure alignment at each coupling while the machine is at operating temperature.
options.D: Record the cold alignment values and assume they remain valid because steel expansion is predictable.

explanation: Thermal growth changes shaft positions as the machine reaches operating temperature, and the actual hot alignment can differ significantly from the cold pre-startup alignment. The correct method is to measure alignment directly at operating temperature using optical tools or dial indicators with the machine at thermal equilibrium, which is typically after 4 or more hours of full-load running. Measuring immediately after shutdown is inaccurate because the machine begins cooling the moment it stops, so readings will not represent the true running condition.

question: A three-stage gearbox has individual gear ratios of 4:1, 5:1, and 3:1 from input to output. The motor delivers 50 Newton-metres of torque to the input shaft. Assuming 100% gearbox efficiency for this calculation, what is the output torque?

options.A: 600 Nm, because the overall ratio is 12:1 multiplied by the 50 Nm input torque.
options.B: 750 Nm, because the output ratio is 15:1 multiplied by the 50 Nm input torque.
options.D: 200 Nm, because the output torque equals input torque multiplied by the average of the three ratios.

explanation: The overall gear ratio of a multi-stage gearbox is found by multiplying all individual stage ratios together: 4 multiplied by 5 multiplied by 3 equals 60. Output torque equals input torque multiplied by the overall ratio: 50 Nm multiplied by 60 equals 3,000 Nm. In a real gearbox, mechanical efficiency losses would reduce this value, typically by 1 to 3% per stage.

question: A millwright is about to start up a recently installed mechanical seal on a process water pump. Before starting the pump, what installation checks must be performed to confirm the mechanical seal is correctly assembled?

options.A: Check that the pump rotation direction arrow matches the motor nameplate and that both are pointing the same way.
options.B: Verify rotating face orientation, confirm mating face is square in the gland, check drive pins are engaged, and inspect that all O-rings are seated without rolling or pinching.
options.C: Measure the stuffing box bore diameter and compare it to the seal cartridge OD to confirm a press fit.
options.D: Confirm that the seal chamber is completely dry before startup because water in the chamber damages the seal faces on first rotation.

explanation: Before starting a pump with a new mechanical seal, four key checks must be completed: the rotating seal face must be correctly oriented (carbon-rotating face toward the mating face), the stationary mating face must be square and flush in the gland plate, the drive pins or drive lugs must be engaged with the rotating face carrier to ensure the rotating face turns with the shaft, and all O-rings must be seated flat in their grooves without rolling or pinching. The seal chamber must be flushed and filled with liquid before startup to prevent dry running which destroys seal faces within seconds.

question: A millwright is calculating the minimum pipe bore for a new process water line carrying 300 litres per minute. The design specification requires fluid velocity to stay below 3 metres per second to control erosion. What is the minimum pipe bore required?

options.A: 25mm minimum bore, which is sufficient for the required flow at the maximum velocity.
options.B: 36mm minimum bore, calculated from flow area equals flow rate divided by velocity.
options.C: 46mm minimum bore, calculated from flow area equals flow rate divided by velocity giving 0.00167 square metres.
options.D: 60mm minimum bore.

explanation: The minimum pipe cross-sectional area is calculated by dividing the volumetric flow rate by the maximum velocity: 300 LPM equals 0.005 cubic metres per second; dividing by 3 m/s gives 0.00167 square metres of required area. From area equals pi times radius squared, radius equals the square root of (0.00167 divided by pi), giving a radius of 0.023m and a diameter of 0.046m or 46mm. The millwright selects the next standard pipe size above 46mm nominal bore to ensure velocity stays below the 3 m/s limit.

question: A millwright must replace a worn conveyor drive chain during a planned 4-hour shutdown. The conveyor has been running with the old chain and matching sprockets. What is the correct replacement procedure, and must the sprockets also be replaced?

options.A: Replace the chain only and reuse the old sprockets to save time and cost during the shutdown.
options.B: Lock out the drive, mark the chain travel direction, replace chain and sprockets together, re-tension, verify guard reinstallation.
options.C: Replace only the most worn sprocket and install the new chain without removing the drive guard.
options.D: Lubricate the old chain with fresh grease and defer replacement to the next shutdown to save time.

explanation: When replacing a drive chain, the sprockets must be replaced at the same time because worn sprocket teeth develop a hook profile that matches the elongated pitch of the worn chain; installing a new chain on worn sprockets causes immediate accelerated wear on the new chain as it tries to seat on the worn tooth profile. The chain travel direction must be marked before removal because a chain run in one direction develops a wear pattern on the link plates and must be reinstalled in the same direction if reused. After assembly, re-tensioning and guard reinstallation are mandatory before returning the conveyor to service.

question: A millwright is replacing a hydraulic directional control valve on a production press. Five hoses connect to the valve ports. What steps must be followed to ensure correct reassembly and safe return to service?

options.A: Photograph the hose layout, relieve system pressure, remove hoses in any order, install new valve, reconnect hoses by matching colours.
options.B: Have a second millwright hold the hoses in position while the first swaps the valve body to avoid losing the port assignments.
options.C: Close the main system shutoff valve, remove the old valve, connect hoses to the new valve matching port size, then restart the system.
options.D: Relieve system pressure, tag out, mark all hose positions, cap all ports, install new valve in same orientation, reconnect hoses to correct ports, bleed and cycle.

explanation: Before removing any hydraulic hose the system must be fully depressurized and the machine locked out and tagged out to prevent unintended cylinder movement. All five hose connections must be marked with their port designations before removal because valve port labeling may differ between manufacturers even for the same valve function. All open ports on both the valve and the hoses must be immediately capped to prevent contamination from entering the system, and after reassembly the system must be bled and cycled at low pressure to confirm correct valve operation and check for leaks before returning to production.

question: A millwright is selecting cushion type for a horizontal pneumatic cylinder moving a 300 kg load at 0.8 metres per second and decelerating within the last 50mm of stroke. Fixed cushions on the existing cylinder are bottoming out hard. What cushion type should be specified, and why?

options.A: Increase supply pressure to slow the cylinder down through added resistance rather than changing the cushion type.
options.B: An adjustable needle-valve cushion, which allows field tuning of deceleration force to match the actual load and speed.
options.C: Remove the cushion and add an external shock absorber mounted on the cylinder end cap bracket.
options.D: A fixed orifice cushion with a smaller orifice diameter to create more deceleration force automatically.

explanation: Fixed cushions provide a predetermined deceleration profile that cannot be tuned once manufactured; when a fixed cushion bottoms out hard it means the orifice is too large and not decelerating the load sufficiently. An adjustable cushion with a needle valve allows the millwright to tune the deceleration force in the field by turning the needle in to restrict exhaust flow from the cushion pocket until the cylinder decelerates smoothly within the 50mm cushion length without bottoming. This adjustability is especially valuable when load mass or speed may vary during production.

question: A press line ran for 20 hours of planned production time in a shift. It was down for 2 hours of unplanned breakdowns. For the 18 hours running, speed was 90% of rated for the first 2 hours and 100% for the remaining 16 hours. The quality reject rate was 3% across the full shift. What is the Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) for this shift?

options.A: OEE is 78.3%, calculated from availability 90%, performance 97.8%, quality 97%.
options.B: OEE is 90.0%.
options.C: OEE is 86.3%, calculated from availability 90%, performance 98.9%, quality 97%.
options.D: OEE is 81.0%, calculated from availability 90%, performance 90%, quality 100%.

explanation: Availability equals actual running time divided by planned time: 18 divided by 20 equals 0.90 or 90%. Performance is weighted by time: 16 hours at 100% plus 2 hours at 90% divided by 18 hours gives 17.8 divided by 18 equals 0.989 or approximately 98.9%. Quality equals good parts divided by total parts: 1 minus 0.03 equals 0.97 or 97%. OEE equals 0.90 multiplied by 0.989 multiplied by 0.97, which equals approximately 0.863 or 86.3%.

question: A millwright is reviewing a pump performance curve to determine whether the pump is operating in its preferred operating range. The pump has a best efficiency point at 380 LPM. The current production flow meter reads 240 LPM. Is this pump in its preferred operating range?

options.A: Yes, the pump is in the preferred range because 240 LPM is above the minimum flow for any centrifugal pump.
options.B: No, the pump is operating at 63% of BEP flow, which is below the typical preferred range of 70% to 120% of BEP.
options.C: Yes, the pump is in the preferred range because any flow that produces adequate discharge pressure is acceptable.
options.D: No, the pump is operating at 63% of BEP but is acceptable provided the vibration level is below 2.5 mm/s RMS.

explanation: The preferred operating region for a centrifugal pump is typically defined as 70% to 120% of the best efficiency point flow. At 240 LPM with a BEP of 380 LPM, the actual flow is 240 divided by 380, which equals 0.632 or 63% of BEP. This is below the lower boundary of the preferred range, meaning the pump is operating in a zone where internal recirculation, hydraulic instability, and elevated radial loads can damage impeller vanes, wear rings, and shaft seals over time. A minimum flow bypass or a change in operating conditions is needed to move the pump into its preferred range.

question: A millwright is planning the installation sequence for a new centrifugal pump and motor set on a grouted baseplate. Which sequence correctly orders the key steps from start to finish to ensure a successful installation?

options.A: Set pump and motor, connect piping, align coupling, grout baseplate, install guard, start.
options.B: Check baseplate level, grout, set pump and motor, rough align, connect piping, precision align, check pipe strain, finalize alignment, install guard, start.
options.C: Grout baseplate first, then level baseplate, set pump, connect all piping, then perform alignment as a single step.
options.D: Set pump and motor, precision align, grout baseplate, connect piping, recheck alignment, install guard, start.

explanation: The baseplate must be levelled and grouted before equipment is set so that grout provides full, stable support under all feet. Rough alignment is done before connecting piping so that pipe connections do not force the equipment into position, which causes pipe strain that shifts alignment under operating load. Precision alignment is performed after piping is connected with zero pipe strain, and is verified before the coupling guard is installed and the unit is started.

question: A millwright has installed a new mechanical seal on a centrifugal pump and is preparing the pump for its first start. Before the pump is started and pressurized, what items must be verified to confirm the mechanical seal is correctly installed?

options.A: Verify that the gland bolts are torqued to the maximum value listed in the torque chart and the pump is filled with water.
options.B: Check that the rotating seal face orientation matches the manufacturer drawing, the stationary face is square in the gland plate, drive pins are engaged, and all O-rings are seated without rolling.
options.C: Confirm the seal flush line is connected and flowing, then start the pump briefly to check for leakage before shutdown.
options.D: Only verify the gland plate is evenly tightened; internal face orientation is set at the factory and should not be adjusted.

explanation: The rotating seal face must be oriented as shown in the manufacturer's drawing because installing it backwards prevents the spring from loading the faces together, resulting in immediate leakage at start-up. The stationary face must sit perfectly square in the gland to ensure even contact across the full face width, and drive pins must engage their slots so the stationary face cannot spin with the shaft. O-rings that are twisted or rolled will extrude under pressure and leak, so each O-ring must be confirmed seated flat in its groove before assembly is completed.

question: A cooling tower that previously maintained process water at 28 degrees Celsius is now only achieving 35 degrees Celsius despite the same ambient conditions and process heat load. What components should the millwright investigate to diagnose this performance decline?

options.A: Replace the fan motor because electric motors are always the first component to degrade in tower performance.
options.B: Check fill media for fouling or blockage, inspect fan blade pitch and balance, verify basin cleanliness.
options.C: Increase the water flow rate through the tower to compensate for the reduced cooling efficiency.
options.D: Check only the inlet louver condition because blocked louvers are the single most common cause of tower performance loss.

explanation: Fill media fouling with scale, biological growth, or debris is one of the most common causes of gradual cooling tower performance decline because it reduces the air-to-water contact surface area available for evaporative cooling. Fan blade pitch controls airflow volume through the tower, and a blade that has shifted or is out of balance delivers less air than designed, directly reducing heat rejection capacity. Basin contamination reduces available water and water treatment failures allow scale and biofilm to coat heat transfer surfaces throughout the tower, compounding the loss.

question: A millwright has added a new hydraulic actuator to an existing circuit. The relief valve setting must now be reviewed to ensure it is still appropriate for the highest load-induced pressure in the updated system. What is the correct procedure for resetting the relief valve?

options.A: Set the relief valve to the pump maximum pressure rating so the full pump output is always available to any actuator.
options.B: Set the relief valve at the new actuator's minimum operating pressure to protect it from overpressure.
options.C: Leave the relief valve at its current setting because adding an actuator does not change the maximum system pressure.
options.D: Determine the maximum load-induced pressure for all actuators in the circuit, then adjust the relief valve to 10 to 15 percent above the highest load-induced pressure and re-seal the adjustment.

explanation: The relief valve must be set above the maximum pressure required to move any actuator against its maximum load, otherwise the relief valve will bypass flow before the actuator develops enough force to do useful work. Setting the relief 10 to 15 percent above the highest load-induced pressure provides a pressure margin that accommodates dynamic pressure spikes and load variations without unnecessarily bypassing oil to tank and generating heat. The adjustment must be re-sealed or locked after setting to prevent unauthorized changes that could result in overpressure damage to system components.

question: A millwright is replacing a hydraulic pump on a gear-driven power unit. The new pump is identical to the failed unit. What must be confirmed and done before the pump is started for the first time after installation?

options.A: Connect all lines, fill the reservoir, and start the pump immediately at full speed to prime the system as quickly as possible.
options.B: Confirm the pump rotation direction matches the arrow on the pump body, fill the case drain port with clean hydraulic oil before starting, and jog the prime mover briefly before running continuously.
options.C: Bleed all air from the pressure lines before starting to prevent hydraulic hammer during first stroke.
options.D: Set the relief valve to minimum before starting and increase pressure gradually over the first hour of operation.

explanation: Hydraulic pump rotation direction must match the direction stamped or marked on the pump body because a fixed-displacement gear or vane pump will attempt to pump backward if rotated the wrong way, which can damage internal seals and bypass valves and will not build system pressure. The case drain cavity must be filled with clean hydraulic oil before the first start because piston and vane pump bearings and internal components rely on this oil film for lubrication before the pump builds enough pressure to circulate oil, and a dry start even for a few seconds can destroy the pump. Jogging allows the operator to confirm rotation direction and listen for correct pump engagement before full-speed continuous operation.

question: A millwright is using the 5-Whys method to perform root cause analysis on a recurring mechanical seal failure on a centrifugal pump that has failed three times in the past year. Tracing the failure chain, the investigation finds the seal face overheated because the flush flow was insufficient, because the flush orifice was plugged, because there is no strainer on the flush line. What is the correct corrective action?

options.A: Replace the mechanical seal with a higher temperature-rated face material to survive the existing overheating condition.
options.B: Install a Y-type strainer on the flush line upstream of the orifice to prevent debris from plugging the orifice, which eliminates the root cause of the failure chain.
options.C: Increase the flush line supply pressure so that particles are blown through the orifice rather than plugging it.
options.D: Replace the fixed orifice with an adjustable needle valve so the flush flow can be increased each time seals begin to overheat.

explanation: The 5-Whys analysis has identified that the absence of a strainer on the flush line is the root cause that allows the orifice to plug, which is the true origin of the entire failure chain. Installing a Y-type strainer upstream of the flush orifice removes the root cause by preventing the debris that plugs the orifice from reaching it in the first place. Replacing or upgrading the seal without correcting the flush system would allow the same failure chain to repeat, while a strainer converts a recurring expensive failure into a routine low-cost strainer cleaning task on the PM program.

question: During shaft alignment on a motor-pump set, the millwright finds the motor shaft is 0.30mm higher than the pump shaft centerline and 0.15mm to the left of the pump shaft centerline at the coupling face. What corrections must be made to the motor position to achieve alignment?

options.A: Add 0.30mm shim under all motor feet and shift motor 0.15mm to the right.
options.B: Remove 0.30mm shim from all motor feet and shift motor 0.15mm to the right.
options.C: Remove 0.15mm shim from all motor feet and shift motor 0.30mm to the left.
options.D: Add 0.15mm shim under front feet only and shift motor 0.30mm to the right.

explanation: If the motor shaft sits 0.30mm too high, removing 0.30mm of shim from under all four feet brings it down to match the pump centerline. If the motor shaft is 0.15mm to the left, the motor must be shifted 0.15mm to the right to center it on the pump shaft. Both corrections must be applied and alignment re-verified before coupling the shafts.

question: A millwright is developing a bearing inspection checklist for a monthly PM route on a packaging line. The route covers 20 grease-lubricated pillow block bearings. Which set of checks must be performed at each bearing location to meet a basic predictive maintenance standard?

options.A: Check bearing temperature, listen for abnormal noise, inspect grease nipple condition, check for leaks, and record all readings.
options.B: Remove bearing cap, inspect rolling elements visually, repack with fresh grease, and reinstall cap.
options.C: Apply grease at nipple until old grease purges, record date, and move to next bearing.
options.D: Replace all bearings on the route every six months regardless of condition readings.

explanation: A proper monthly PM route uses non-invasive condition monitoring: temperature (via IR thermometer), sound (via stethoscope or ultrasound probe), grease nipple condition, and leak check. Recording each reading creates a trend baseline so changes over time trigger corrective action before failure occurs. Removing caps or replacing parts unnecessarily on every PM introduces contamination risk and wastes parts.

question: A millwright completes a mechanical seal replacement on a centrifugal pump. Before the pump is started, a pre-startup checklist must be completed. Which step is most commonly missed and can cause immediate seal damage if skipped?

options.A: Verifying the coupling guard is painted and free of rust before installation.
options.B: Filling and venting the pump casing to remove air before starting the motor.
options.C: Measuring the pump impeller diameter to confirm it matches the order sheet.
options.D: Confirming the motor current reading matches the motor nameplate full-load amps.

explanation: Running a centrifugal pump dry, even for a few seconds, will destroy the mechanical seal because the seal faces rely on the process liquid for lubrication and cooling. Filling and venting the casing removes trapped air so the seal is lubricated from the first rotation. Other checklist steps matter but a dry-run failure happens immediately and ruins a just-installed seal.

question: A millwright plans a lift inside a building with 8 metres of clear headroom. The load stands 1.8 metres tall, the chain hoist body is 0.6 metres deep, the sling from hook to load is 1.5 metres, and the hook approach from the trolley to the hook is 0.5 metres. Is there enough headroom to complete the lift?

options.A: No, the total headroom required is 5.9 metres, which exceeds the 8 metre clearance available.
options.B: Cannot be determined without knowing the load weight and the hoist rated capacity.
options.C: Yes, but only if the sling length is reduced to 1.0 metre to create additional clearance margin.
options.D: Yes, the total headroom required is 4.4 metres, which is well within the 8 metre clearance.

explanation: Headroom required equals load height plus sling length plus hoist body depth plus hook approach: 1.8 plus 1.5 plus 0.6 plus 0.5 equals 4.4 metres total. The building has 8 metres of clear height, so there is 3.6 metres of margin above the minimum required headroom. The lift can proceed without any modification to the rigging arrangement, and load weight does not affect headroom requirements.

question: A millwright is performing a fan impeller balance check after weld repair. The impeller is mounted on a balance arbor and the heavy spot is marked. Test weights are added opposite the heavy spot in a series of trial runs. When is the balancing job complete?

options.A: When the impeller spins freely with no wobble visible to the naked eye at slow rotation speed.
options.B: When the residual imbalance is within the G6.3 balance grade for the impeller operating speed.
options.C: When the added test weight equals 10 percent of the total impeller weight at the correction radius.
options.D: When vibration at the bearing pedestals reads below 5mm per second RMS at operating speed.

explanation: ISO 1940 balance quality grades define acceptable residual imbalance as a function of rotor mass, operating speed, and the service class of the rotor. G6.3 is the standard grade for fans and blowers, and the allowed residual imbalance in gram-millimetres is calculated from the grade number, the rotor mass, and the service speed. Balancing to a visible standard or an arbitrary weight fraction does not guarantee the impeller meets the engineering specification needed to prevent bearing damage at operating speed.

question: A millwright measures keyway width on a shaft that will accept a standard key. The drawing calls out the shaft keyway as D10 tolerance and the hub keyway as H9 tolerance. The measured shaft keyway is at the middle of the D10 range. What does this mean for the fit between the key and the shaft?

options.A: The key will have clearance fit in the shaft keyway, which is the intended design for shaft keyways.
options.B: The key will be an interference fit in the shaft keyway, which prevents the key from being installed.
options.C: The key will be a transition fit; the installer must press it in with a hydraulic press.
options.D: The shaft keyway is undersized and must be broached wider before the key can be fitted.

explanation: ISO keyway tolerances are deliberately chosen so the key is a snug but not interference fit in the shaft: D10 on the shaft keyway provides a slight clearance that allows the key to slide in by hand while still being held tightly once the hub is installed. The hub keyway in H9 is a tighter fit so the key is driven into the hub. This arrangement means the key can be installed without special tools and the drive torque is transmitted through the sides of the key, not by a press fit between key and shaft.

question: Oil analysis on a gearbox on a 6-month change interval shows that viscosity is within 8 percent of new oil, wear metals are below alarm limits, and water content is below detection. The maintenance team must decide the next oil change interval. What is the appropriate decision?

options.A: Change the oil immediately because the 6-month interval has elapsed regardless of oil condition.
options.B: Run the gearbox without further oil analysis because the initial sample confirmed it is in good condition.
options.C: Drain and replace the oil within 2 weeks to prevent the viscosity from dropping further.
options.D: Extend the interval to 9 months, resample at that point, and change only if any parameter goes out of limits.

explanation: Oil analysis is used precisely to replace oil based on condition rather than a fixed calendar interval, reducing unnecessary oil changes and downtime while catching real degradation early. When all parameters are within acceptable ranges, extending the interval and retesting is the evidence-based decision. Changing perfectly good oil at a fixed interval wastes money and oil, and introduces contamination risk from the oil-change procedure itself.

question: A millwright is replacing an oil seal on a gearbox output shaft. After removing the old seal, the housing bore is inspected and found to be clean with no scoring. What is the correct sequence for installing the new seal?

options.A: Lubricate the seal OD with grease, place seal over shaft by hand, tap around the edge with a hammer until flush.
options.B: Clean the bore, install new seal using a seal driver centered on the bore, press to specified depth, verify sealing lip direction.
options.C: Install the new seal by threading it over the shaft keyway, then press the outer edge down with a flat bar.
options.D: Apply RTV sealant around the seal OD before pressing in to compensate for any bore surface irregularities.

explanation: A seal driver that matches the seal OD applies uniform pressing force around the full circumference of the seal case, preventing the seal from cocking in the bore. The seal must be pressed to the depth specified in the OEM procedure, which is typically flush with the housing face or a stated dimension below it. Verifying that the sealing lip faces the fluid side (inward toward the gear oil) before pressing confirms the seal will work correctly; a reversed lip allows oil to escape past the shaft.

question: A drawing note reads 'NPS 4 SCH 80' for a process pipe. A new millwright asks whether the nominal pipe size of 4 means the pipe's outside diameter is 4 inches. What is the actual outside diameter, and how does NPS relate to actual pipe dimensions?

options.A: OD is exactly 4.000 inches; NPS always matches the outside diameter precisely.
options.B: OD is 4.500 inches; NPS is a nominal designation and does not equal the actual OD.
options.C: OD is 4.250 inches; NPS equals the inside diameter for schedule 80 pipe only.
options.D: OD is 5.000 inches; schedule number determines the outside diameter of the pipe.

explanation: NPS 4 pipe has a standardized outside diameter of 4.500 inches (114.3 mm) regardless of schedule, and NPS 4 SCH 80 has a wall thickness of 0.337 inches (8.56 mm). NPS is a nominal designation used for identification and compatibility purposes only and does not equal the actual outside diameter. The schedule number determines wall thickness, while the outside diameter stays fixed for a given NPS.

question: A millwright needs to lift a 2,000 kg gearbox using a single hoist attachment point. The sling angle from vertical will be approximately 40 degrees due to the rigging arrangement. The available options are a fixed eyebolt rated for vertical lift and a swivel hoist ring with an equivalent vertical rating. Which attachment should be selected and why?

options.A: Fixed eyebolt.
options.B: Swivel hoist ring.
options.C: Plate lifting clamp with a vertical jaw.
options.D: Either device.

explanation: A fixed eyebolt loaded at an angle below 45 degrees from vertical suffers a significant reduction in its working load limit, sometimes dropping to less than 30 percent of the vertical rating, because the eye is not designed to handle angular loading efficiently. A swivel hoist ring rotates and pivots to align itself with the resultant sling force, allowing it to maintain close to its full rated capacity regardless of sling angle. For any lift where the sling angle is not perfectly vertical, the swivel hoist ring is the correct and safer choice.

question: A signal person must direct a crane operator to move a suspended load diagonally across the work area, requiring simultaneous bridge and trolley movement. A coworker states that diagonal travel is not permitted for safety reasons. Is diagonal travel allowed, and what conditions must be met?

options.A: Diagonal travel is prohibited in all facilities because the load will swing uncontrollably during combined motion.
options.B: Diagonal travel is allowed if both motions are controlled and the load does not pendulum.
options.C: Diagonal travel is allowed only if the load weighs less than 50 percent of the crane rated capacity.
options.D: Diagonal travel requires a written lift plan regardless of load weight or travel distance.

explanation: Diagonal travel using simultaneous bridge and trolley motion is permitted when both motions remain under control and the load does not begin to pendulum or swing away from the intended path. The signal person communicates both simultaneous motions to the operator using combined hand signals or radio communication, and the operator must be able to stop either motion independently if the load begins to drift. If the load starts to pendulum, one or both motions must be stopped immediately to allow the load to stabilize.

question: A millwright is re-greasing a large pillow block bearing that has been in service. The grease vent plug has been left in place by the previous maintenance worker. Describe the correct grease purge procedure and explain what happens if the vent plug is not removed before greasing.

options.A: Remove the inlet fitting, force grease in through the vent, and reinstall the inlet when done.
options.B: Leave the vent plug in place, pump until resistance increases, and stop immediately at resistance.
options.C: Remove the vent plug, connect the grease gun to the inlet, pump slowly, stop when fresh grease exits the vent.
options.D: Replace both the inlet and vent fittings with new ones before applying any grease to the bearing.

explanation: The correct procedure is to remove the vent plug before greasing so that old contaminated grease and excess pressure have a path to escape from the bearing housing. Fresh grease is pumped in slowly through the inlet until new grease appears at the open vent, confirming that old grease has been purged and the bearing cavity contains fresh lubricant. If the vent plug is left in during greasing, pressure builds inside the bearing housing and can damage seals, force grease past the seals into the machine, or collapse the seal entirely.

question: A millwright is tensioning a V-belt drive on a mobile machine that operates in a high-vibration environment. Two options are available: a static tensioning arrangement using an adjustable motor base and lock bolts, or an automatic spring-loaded belt tensioner. Which option should be selected and why?

options.A: Static tensioning using lock bolts.
options.B: Either method provides equal performance in high-vibration applications on mobile equipment.
options.C: Static tensioning.
options.D: Automatic spring-loaded tensioner.

explanation: In a high-vibration environment, the constant movement of the machine causes lock bolts on a static tensioning arrangement to work loose over time, allowing belt tension to drop and increasing the risk of belt slip, wear, and premature failure. An automatic spring-loaded belt tensioner continuously adjusts to maintain the correct belt tension regardless of the vibration-induced movement of the machine frame. This makes the spring tensioner the correct and more reliable choice for mobile equipment applications where re-tensioning after every shift would otherwise be required.

question: A hydraulic motor coupling failed by shearing through the keyway that connected the coupling hub to the motor shaft. The millwright must determine the root cause and recommend a design change to prevent a repeat failure. What is the most likely cause and the correct recommendation?

options.A: The key was made of the wrong material; replace with a stainless steel key of the same size.
options.B: The keyway created a stress concentration that initiated the fracture; use a spline or larger key.
options.C: The coupling was over-tightened on the shaft; reduce the hub interference fit on replacement.
options.D: The motor was undersized for the application; replace with a motor of double the rated torque.

explanation: A keyway machined into a shaft creates a sharp stress concentration at the corner of the keyway slot, which significantly reduces the fatigue strength of the shaft at that location under cyclic torsional loading. This stress concentration is the initiation point for torsional fatigue cracks that eventually cause failure through the keyway, especially in applications with reversing or shock loads such as hydraulic motor drives. The correct corrective design is to use a splined shaft connection, which distributes the torque over many contact surfaces and eliminates the single stress concentration point.

question: A millwright is installing a new flex disc coupling and must torque the flex element bolts to the OEM specification of 45 Nm. A coworker suggests that the bolts just need to feel tight and a calibrated torque wrench is not necessary for this type of coupling. What problem can result from unevenly torqued flex disc bolts?

options.A: No problem results because flex disc couplings self-equalize bolt loads during operation.
options.B: Uneven torque causes uneven loading on the flex disc, leading to premature disc fatigue failure.
options.C: Bolts that are too tight will strip the threads, and this is the only torque-related risk.
options.D: Overtorqued bolts compress the disc too much, and this is corrected automatically during break-in.

explanation: A flex disc coupling transmits torque through a flexible disc element that is clamped between alternating drive and driven bolts. If the clamping bolts are not all torqued to the same value, some sections of the disc experience more clamping force than others, creating uneven stress distribution across the disc during rotation. This uneven loading causes one section of the disc to flex more than the rest, concentrating fatigue cycles at that location and causing premature cracking and failure of the flex element, even within a relatively short service period.

question: A millwright selects a replacement bearing from the parts room. The original bearing number was 6309-C3. The parts room has a 6309 without a clearance code. Before installing the replacement, what must the millwright verify, and why does the C3 designation matter?

options.A: C3 is a grease type designation; verify the bearing is pre-greased before installation.
options.B: C3 designates greater internal radial clearance; a standard bearing may seize under the same operating conditions.
options.C: C3 indicates the bearing was made in Canada; any equivalent bearing from another country is acceptable.
options.D: C3 means the bearing is sealed; verify the replacement has the same seal type before installing.

explanation: The C3 suffix on a bearing designation indicates a greater-than-normal internal radial clearance between the rolling elements and the races. Bearings specified with C3 clearance are required in applications where the bearing will run hot (causing the inner race to expand onto the shaft) or where fits are tighter than normal, both of which reduce internal clearance during operation. Installing a standard clearance bearing in an application designed for C3 clearance can result in zero or negative internal clearance during operation, causing the bearing to run with excessive preload and overheat, leading to premature failure.

question: A millwright is installing a new chain sprocket that requires an interference fit on the shaft. The hub bore is 80.00 mm and the shaft diameter is 80.05 mm, giving 0.05 mm interference. The OEM manual specifies heating the hub to 120 degrees Celsius for installation. What is the correct installation procedure and why must the hub cool completely before loading?
